title: Oil Spill Reaches UAE Beaches and Moves Toward Turtle Islands
summary:
Oil is spreading along the coast of the United Arab Emirates. At some beaches, the water has turned black.

The oil is leaking from a tanker called Gem No.2. The ship was damaged on October 9 near the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway many oil tankers pass through. A maritime company said the ship was hit by an unknown projectile and caught fire. The fire was put out, and all 22 crew members were rescued. A small leak was seen on October 19. Later, satellite pictures showed the oil spreading more than 35 kilometres (22 miles).

This week, oil reached beaches near the city of Umm Al Quwain, and some beaches were closed. The government said it began containment right away to limit the harm.

Oil can trap sea turtles, cover the feathers of seabirds, and hurt the gills of fish. The oil is drifting toward protected islands where green turtles live. Experts say it is too early to know how much harm it will cause.
why_it_matters: Oil in the sea can close beaches where families swim and hurt the turtles, birds, and fish that live there.
